text: International Coconut Conference to unlock new growth opportunities for Việt Nam coconut industry

VĨNH LONG - The CocoNext 2026 International Coconut Conference will take place in Vĩnh Long Province on December 12-13, providing a platform for domestic and international stakeholders to explore ways to increase the value and competitiveness of Việt Nam's coconut industry.

The event, which will have the theme "Synergising the Coconut Value Chain to Accelerate Sustainable Growth", will be hosted by the Vĩnh Long People's Committee, with Bến Tre Import Export Joint Stock Corporation (Betrimex) acting as initiator and organiser.
It is expected to attract more than 500 delegates, including government officials, scientists, business executives, financial institutions, and international partners.

Speaking at a press conference in Vĩnh Long on November 17 to introduce CocoNext 2026, Trần Trí Quang, chairman of the provincial People's Committee, said coconuts had long been an important part of the Mekong Delta's economy and culture.

"For Vĩnh Long, coconut is not only an economically valuable crop but also a key agricultural commodity, playing an important role in developing the processing industry, boosting exports, creating jobs and improving local livelihoods.
Following the provincial reorganisation, the province now has more than 121,000 hectares of coconut farms, or around 60 per cent of the country's total.
This gives it great potential to develop large-scale coconut-growing areas and become a hub of the country's coconut industry.

However, the province wants to do more than expand cultivation and increase output, and is also seeking to improve productivity and value per hectare, develop higher-value processing, diversify products, build brands, and expand into international markets.

"We need to shift from agricultural production thinking to an agricultural economy approach, and from exporting raw materials and semi-processed products to developing goods with higher technological content, added value and competitiveness," he said.
He added that the industry should make better use of every part of the coconut, including its water, flesh, husk, shell, and other by-products, to develop a green, circular, and sustainable economy.

CocoNext 2026 was expected to encourage cooperation between government agencies, researchers, businesses, and international partners, while promoting new technologies, digital transformation, and innovation, he said.
The programme on December 12 will have three sessions focusing on the national vision for the coconut industry, global trade and soft power, and sustainable technology and the circular economy.

Discussions will cover market trends, digital transformation in coconut-growing areas, higher-value processing, supply chain financing, zero-waste production, biotechnology, and the potential for generating carbon credits from coconut ecosystems.
An exhibition on the sidelines will showcase technologies for coconut cultivation, plantation management, higher-value processing, and measuring environmental value.
The CocoNext 2026 Synergy Space will have 36 booths for business networking and showcasing coconut products and the province's key initiatives.

On December 13, delegates will visit the Betrimex factory in Lương Hoà, the Hương Mỹ coconut-growing area, the Coconut Nectar Factory in Tiểu Cần, and the Wax Coconut Museum in Tam Ngãi, experiencing the full coconut value chain ranging from raw material zones and deep-processing technologies to multi-value models, gene conservation, and indigenous knowledge preservation.

According to Đặng Huỳnh Ức My, chairwoman of Betrimex, coconuts offer opportunities across a wide range of industries, including food, beverages, confectionery, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, handicrafts, activated carbon, and renewable energy.

At CocoNext, Betrimex will present a modern coconut value chain built around five interconnected areas: identifying market opportunities, investing in higher-value processing and making use of by-products, standardising cultivation areas and traceability, applying nutritional science to product development, and developing supply chain financing.
The company is committed to helping Việt Nam build a coconut industry with the potential to generate billions of dollars in exports.

Quang said he hoped CocoNext 2026 would produce more than discussions, leading to new initiatives, investment projects, and practical partnerships that would increase incomes for coconut growers and strengthen Việt Nam's position in the global market. - VNS
